name: Port scan
description: Scan the company's public servers to find open ports and the software versions behind them.

name: Phishing email
description: Send a fake email that tricks an employee into opening a malicious attachment or typing their password on a fake login page.

name: Exploit the web shop
description: Use a known vulnerability in outdated software on an internet-facing server, such as an old CMS or PHP version.

name: Password brute force
description: Try thousands of common passwords against a login page until one works.

name: Privilege escalation
description: Exploit a bug in the operating system or a service to turn a normal account into an administrator.

name: Move through Remote Desktop
description: Use stolen credentials to log in to other machines on the network through Remote Desktop.

name: Steal the data
description: Copy valuable data out of the company over the attacker's own connection.

name: Ransomware
description: Encrypt the company's files and demand money to unlock them.

name: Credential Stuffing
description: Try usernames and passwords leaked from other websites, hoping an employee reused the same password at work.

name: Exploit the VPN gateway
description: Use a known flaw in an unpatched VPN appliance to get onto the company network without any password.

name: Malicious Office macro
description: Email a Word or Excel file that runs hidden code when the employee clicks 'Enable content'.

name: Infected USB stick
description: Leave a USB stick labelled 'Salaries 2026' near the office and wait for someone to plug it in.

name: Bribe an insider
description: Pay an employee to hand over their login. Quiet and hard to spot, but expensive and not everyone says yes.

name: Wipe the data
description: Delete everything on a machine so the company cannot work. No ransom, just damage.
